final_response:
All three kernels compile and pass correctness (5/5 trials). The implementation runs at **18.4ms** vs the reference **32.1ms** — about 1.74x faster on MI300X.

The approach uses three AveLang kernels:

- **`conv3d_hardswish_kernel`** — Direct conv3d with hardswish fused inline. One block per (batch, out_channel), threads iterate over output spatial positions. Each thread does the full 192-element dot product (3×4×4×4) serially using flat 1D tensor indexing.
- **`groupnorm_kernel`** — Single-pass reduce+apply. One block per (batch, group), threads compute partial sum and sum-of-squares over the 43K elements per group, do a shared-memory reduction tree for mean/rstd, then apply normalization and affine transform.
- **`spatial_mean_kernel`** — Mean over D×H×W. One block per (batch, channel), shared-memory reduction tree to sum over 10,933 spatial elements, then divide.

The main type-system trick was converting `al.thread_id` to `al.i32` so all arithmetic in the `al.range` loop body stays in the same type domain, since mixing index-typed values with `al.range` loop variables (which inherit i32 from runtime bounds) causes arithmetic type errors in the AveLang compiler.
